heading: The conversation about flaws (a section of an essay on romance and relationships, after a section on getting to know someone through card games and social gatherings)

texts.for: opens the section: you can't learn everything from card games and gatherings, yet asking straight out about someone's mistakes in past relationships would be an odd thing to do on a date
texts.text: Card games and social gatherings don’t tell you everything, but asking someone out of the blue, “What did you do wrong in your past relationships?” would make for a pretty weird date.

texts.for: what to look at in someone's most recent conflicts to see how they handle trouble: whether they could regulate themselves, what they did and how they repaired it, whether their judgment has improved, and whether their friends or exes would agree
texts.text: Look at the most recent conflicts and ask if you were able to regulate yourself during them. What did you do to the other person, and how did you repair the damage afterward? Has your judgment gotten better, or do you keep falling for the same stuff, and would your friends or exes agree?

texts.for: one example of turning a vague self-description ("I shut down") into what it meant in practice for the partner
texts.text: And if you tell me you shut down, I’d ask whether that meant you stopped talking to your partner for days, and whether they felt abandoned.
